name: Exchange Online Public Folder Exit Pack
problem: Microsoft will not add generic Public Folder CRUD to Microsoft Graph. Third-party EWS access to Exchange Online Public Folders therefore has no direct Graph replacement as EWS is retired.
why_now: EWS is permanently disabled in Exchange Online on 2027-04-01.
Microsoft explicitly lists generic Public Folder CRUD among capabilities that will not be added to Graph.
Backup/sync vendors including Druva, Keepit, SysCloud and CiraSync are publicly warning that Public Folder backup/sync or direct access will stop or must be redesigned.

wedge.offer: Public Folder Exit Assessment + Migration Blueprint
wedge.description: Inventory Public Folder dependencies and classify each workload into shared mailbox, Microsoft 365 Group, SharePoint/Teams, CRM, archive/export, or retire. Deliver mapping, risk, permissions, coexistence and cutover plan without requiring mailbox content by default.
wedge.buyer: Microsoft 365 MSPs, IT departments, backup/sync customers, organizations with legacy shared contacts/calendars/workflows

advantages: The gap cannot be solved by a generic EWS-to-Graph endpoint because Graph intentionally lacks generic Public Folder CRUD.
The deliverable is mostly discovery, classification and migration design, so it can be standardized before building heavy software.
Multiple independent vendors expose the same deadline and unsupported workload, creating observable prospect signals.
competition_and_risk: CodeTwo, BitTitan, CiraSync/CiraHub and specialist Microsoft partners already offer migration tooling or services.
This is a deadline-driven market and will shrink after migrations complete.
A generic migration service is not defensible; distribution through MSPs and an automated assessment/report is the preferred wedge.
next_gate: Find at least 20 recent public signals from organizations/MSPs/vendors mentioning Exchange Online Public Folders plus EWS dependency, backup/sync loss, or migration need; require >=8 commercially plausible channels/prospects before building a public Rockrai experiment.
